**Refined [Draft] Three Values:**

Daring
Honorable
Emergent

Alternatives to Daring:
- Experimental
- Frontier-mentality
- Cutting-edge
- Bold


Alternatives to Honorable:
- Honesty
- Trust
- Pragmatic
- Long-term Thinking
- Good faith


Alternatives to Emergent:
- Community-Owned
- Community-Governance
- Voice
- Federated
- Bottom-up
- Community-Led


**Key thoughts and questions:**
- Consider how these are differentiating us from other projects
- Consider who our target audience is, who are we trying to convert?
- How do these three values interplay with each other?
- Context is important, ie. we’re experimental because we’re on substrate but we’re robust within substrate
- Community film is a way for us to highlight these values
- Want to choose terms which are maximally emotionally evocative
- Consider making these kind of playful, yet evocative - ie. ‘Humane’ vs. ‘Keep It Human’
- When we launch this rebrand, we could also focus on new marketing, re: our positioning as part of Polkadot/Kusama - ICON was interested in that
- We don’t just want a set of three values that are nominally in an employee handbook, on the website but don’t mean anything


**Next steps:**
- Community members quickly give any additional feedback
- Thom and small group incorporate this feedback to finalize a top 3 values
- Workshop associated copy which can be posted alongside the values, ie. on the website, marketing materials
- Create actionable ways to practice these values
- Ie. Emergent means that we identify a list of active, successful contributors to the protocol and an agency member will directly reach out to them to solicit feedback for big branding/partnership decisions
- Ie. Honorable means that we do not tolerate people acting in bad faith. We set expectations around transparency and people executing not only to the letter of their promises but the spirit.

We will be hosting an event on the Discord stage to discuss the results of the survey, **tomorrow at 11 am.** Please drop by if you have any questions, comments, etc. If you cannot attend, you can always weigh-in here. We will take notes.

The hope is to address some of the concerns, criticisms, ideas in this thread and exit the event with a clear next step to finalizing (for now) our top values and actionable ways to bring them into our work.

> Re: edgMesh - this is interesting, but I think we also need more detail on how this compares to other chains, because there are many chains that bring an engaged user base. As a builder, I don't really think having a protocol bring a loosely engaged community is a huge value add to me - I'd rather think in terms of reducing platform risk, reducing governance risk, having access to Polkadot, etc, etc. 

For a purely generic smart contract platform then the community can be loosly tied.

For one with a treasury that is effectively leveraged to advance people and projects in a collective manner, then its absolutely vital to have a well coordinated community. 

So I absolutely understand your priorities - for a builder it makes sense and those are key items, but we are advancing a community here in a way Ethereum could not, since it never had a core network fund. 

The network fund has a gravity to it, that binds people and projects together.

Hi Friends,

I would like to bump this thread.

Thanks for the feedback so far, Rich, raymondz, and Thom.

Does anyone have any other feedback on the survey results or how they would like to proceed? I will be announcing next steps shortly but wanted to add one last call for initial feedback.

In general agreement with Grant's original post. A couple of suggestions:

- Honesty/Trust -> lean towards Trust
- Community-first -> I think there could be more elaboration to figure out what this means in practice. For example, something like "truly decentralized governance process" (we actually have many participants in the community, coming from different backgrounds and with different opinions, and we manage to distill their insights into one end product) would capture what we do differently in a tangible way. We're already doing some of that messaging when we talk about the Agency being a DAO for example.


Re: edgMesh - this is interesting, but I think we also need more detail on how this compares to other chains, because there are many chains that bring an engaged user base. As a builder, I don't really think having a protocol bring a loosely engaged community is a huge value add to me - I'd rather think in terms of reducing platform risk, reducing governance risk, having access to Polkadot, etc, etc.

> The question for me is, what is the mission? On the technical side, CW Labs has championed 'to create an incredible dapp platform to enable open societies,'

Having thought about this a lot for the community film and discussing with the [@Lemonade Money](/edgeware/account/k4iFPUjMULR3faN6Uw4s1UszQT4w9PSSZSFd69Sn8Y6qKjG) team, the key things that stand out from a messaging perspective and also join the dots between a bunch of things and are coherent with the early positioning and also marries well with the evolving Ecosystem Partners strategy.

## Edgeware as an incubator

This was kind of esoteric to start with, because an incubator is by definition defined by the things it incubates. 

We can see 'incubation' through a number of mechanisms and perspectives.

- Incubating people, processes, concepts and bold new thinking
- A space to experiment, to advance young talent
- Treasury funding individuals and projects through the development cycle
- Treasury deployed in a few different ways
- Deploy smart contracts to Edgeware's blockchain in whichever language you prefer and the community will be your first users / dogfooders.
- Parachain / Relay chain / Chain factory
- This is again an incubator approach - spin up small and then scale as a chain


The 'incubator' tagline also plays well into the: **What Will You Build? ** tagline and the way that can morph and evolve depending on context.

## Edgeware as an incubator

This was kind of esoteric to start with, because an incubator is by definition defined by the things it incubates.

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/7d5ff19e-e53d-41c0-bbf6-c35421969308.1623666494596)

In the end the _**disagree and proceed** _line which was proposed by[@dillchen](/edgeware/account/hwJpK8k6Q1KR8F87u5KHfBghRRit7p5UYWC1ubPDwsjdh6s),[@drewstone](/edgeware/account/hwR8hAatmmdupBLXQSxLUPBa8GhRomLD9hf6iRtFeXs8fcY)  and[@raymondz](/straightedge/account/str186wygrqrgykzcr5s0alajur0p2ddc7qe8fxdkz) is ok as an ethos, but it misses perhaps the key point, that we can all build on each others insights, innovations and ideas - in fact this_ community choreography_ is absolutely vital. 

With that in mind the idea of an **EDGmesh** should be a core community philosophy - joining the dots between people and projects, dogfooding each others initiatives, seeing commonalities where others see differences... this is how we end up with a uniquely differentiated stack - the connections between seemingly unrelated concepts, projects and people.

We also need to be open to experimentation - via the incubator concept, but equally we need to be careful around things like the treasury and other common pool resources that should be managed carefully, strategically and conservatively.

body:
I think this was such a valuable exercise - particularly in informing our brand and voice over the next few months. 
I'm increasingly leaning into a warm, open-minded, but mission-oriented presentation for the network in my opinion.

Edgy but competent, open minds but high standards. 

Right now, a lot of our portrayals probably don't match this. The website currently, compared to teams like Plasm, seems a bit too 'kiddy'- where we could clean and sharpen up the presentation more. In my mind we're not as open/do whatever/ dance in fursuits as ETH, but we're also not as ossified as BTC, decred, and we're not as esoteric and opaque as Urbit. 

The question for me is, what is the mission? On the technical side, CW Labs has championed 'to create an incredible dapp platform to enable open societies,' (paraphrase, perhaps) The community for the last several months has focused on the latter half of that phrase, but I do think it captures both stories reasonably well.  I think it would be enhanced by a brief elaboration on that open society concept.
